{{Short description|French neurobiologist and neuropsychiatrist (1935–2024)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2024}}
'''Jean-Didier Vincent''' (7 June 1935 – 4 December 2024) was a French [[neurobiologist]] and [[Neuropsychiatry|neuropsychiatrist]]. He was Professor of [[Physiology]] at the Faculty of Medicine of the [[University of Bordeaux]] II and then at the [[Paris-Sud University|University of Paris-Sud.]] From 1991 to 2004 Vincent was Director of the Alfred-Fessard Institute of [[Neurobiology]] at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. He was a member of both the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Académie Nationale de Médecine|French Academy of Medicine]] since 18 November 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fam.fr/en/academy-of-medicine/|title=The Academy of medicine|website=Fondation de l'Académie de Médecine|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Vincent was born on 7 June 1935 in [[Libourne]], located in the [[Gironde]] department of [[Bordeaux]].<ref>Cf. Acte de naissance n° 266 en date du 7 juin 1935 du registre des naissances de l'état-civil de la ville de Libourne pour l'année 1935; ''Who's who in France'', éd. Jacques Lafitte, 41<sup>e</sup> édition, 2010, page 2203, où encore ''Who's who in Sud-Ouest'', éd. Jacques Lafitte, 1<sup>re</sup> édition, 1987, page 225, où les notices rédigées par l'intéressé lui-même mentionnent bien sa naissance à Libourne. Il n'est donc pas né à Castillon-la-Bataille ou Sainte-Foy-la-Grande, comme l'indiquent à tort divers auteurs de publications le concernant.</ref> He was the only son of a [[Freemasonry|Freemason]] wine broker.<ref name="autobio gen">{{cite web|title=Jean-Didier Vincent, neurobiologiste, publie son autobiographie génétique. Pour lui, "La vie est une fable". L'être et le vivant|url=http://www.liberation.fr/portrait/1998/12/26/jean-didier-vincent-neurobiologiste-publie-son-autobiographie-genetique-pour-lui-la-vie-est-une-fabl_253452|author=Pascale Nivelle|website=Libération.fr|date=26 December 2016|access-date=21 January 2017}}</ref>

He studied in [[Sainte-Foy-la-Grande]] ([[Gironde]]) at a [[Protestantism|Protestant]] college whose master intended him to study literature at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]], then at the Lycée Michel-Montaigne in [[Bordeaux]].<ref name="Autrement">''Chercher - Jours après jours, les aventuriers du savoir'', éditions Autrement, 2000, {{ISBN|9782746700550}}, {{p.|121-123}}.</ref> His parents, wine brokers and Protestants, encouraged him to undertake medical studies<ref name="Autrement" /> at the [[École du service de santé des armées|École du Service de Santé des Armées]] de Bordeaux.<ref name="Teteatete">[http://www.franceculture.fr/emission-le-tete-a-tete-jean-didier-vincent-2012-01-22 Entretien avec Jean-Didier Vincent] dans ''Le Tête-à-tête'' de [[Frédéric Taddeï]] sur [[France Culture]] le 22 janvier 2012.</ref> He majored in [[physics]], [[chemistry]] and [[biology]]. As an intern in clinical services, he met the neuropsychiatrist Jacques Faure, who encouraged him to do research in this field.<ref name="Teteatete" /><ref>Interview de Jean Didier Vincent par Jacques Paugam sur Canal Académie, 27 février 2011</ref>

Vincent was a hospital [[biologist]] in physiology and functional explorations at the CHRU of Bordeaux (1966-1977), Professor without a chair (1973-1978) and professor of physiology at the Bordeaux Faculty of Medicine (1979-1992). He headed the [[Inserm]] 176/CNRS "Neurobiology of Behaviours" unit at the Bordeaux University Hospital (1978-1990) before taking over as Director of the Alfred-Fessart Institute in [[Gif-sur-Yvette]] from 1992 to 2003. He was Professor of Physiology at the Faculty of Medicine of Paris Sud, Hospital Practitioner at the [[Le Kremlin-Bicêtre|Kremlin-Bicêtre]] Hospital (1992-2006) and Professor at the Institut Universitaire de France, Chair of [[Neuroendocrinology]] at the Faculty of Medicine of Paris-Sud, Paris XI University (1994-2004).<ref>[http://histoire.inserm.fr/les-femmes-et-les-hommes/jean-didier-vincent/(page)/2 Jean-Didier Vincent] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203021851/https://histoire.inserm.fr/les-femmes-et-les-hommes/jean-didier-vincent/(page)/2 |date=2019-02-03 }}, sur histoire.inserm.fr</ref>

In 1988, he signed the appeal to [[François Mitterrand]].<ref name="autobio gen" /> He has carried out research in [[neurobiology]] in the United States (postdoctoral fellowship at the Brain Institute of the [[University of California]], Los Angeles) and then in France (CNRS, Inserm).

Vincent was President of the National Council of Programmes at the Ministry of National Education from 2002, a member of the CNRS Ethics of Science Committee (COMETS) and the INRA (Institut National de Recherché en Agronomie) Ethics and Precaution Committee for Agricultural Research Applications (COMEPRA). A member of the Executive Board of the Foundation for Political Innovation until 23 January 2009, he has been President of the Association pour l'Université Numérique Francophone Mondiale (UNFM) since October 2005.{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}

Married to Yveline Ricoul and later to Lucy Kukstas, he had five children. Jean-Didier Vincent died on 4 December 2024, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |title=Le professeur girondin Jean-Didier Vincent, pionnier des neurosciences, est décédé |url=https://www.sudouest.fr/necrologies/le-professeur-girondin-jean-didier-vincent-pionnier-des-neurosciences-est-decede-22396111.php |access-date=4 December 2024 |publisher=Sud Ouest |date=4 December 2024}}</ref>

== Scientific contributions ==
Vincent contributed significantly to the development of [[neuroendocrinology]], which includes the study of interactions between [[hormone]]s and the [[nervous system]], the brain being also considered as an [[endocrine gland]].{{citation needed|date=May 2020}} He has a more pessimistic vision than his colleague [[Boris Cyrulnik]] about what predetermines human behaviour and believes in the primacy of the biological over reason, stating in 2013 in the film ''La Possibilité d'être humain'' : "''L'homme est libre, oui, mais en liberté surveillée''".

He published numerous books on the theory of biology, for example, Biologie des passions, La Chair et le diable.<ref>Sébastien Lemerle, « Les habits neufs du biologisme en France », ''Actes de la recherche en sciences sociale'', <abbr>n<sup>os</sup></abbr> 176-177, 2009, <abbr>p.</abbr> 75</ref> In his book he defends a dynamic above all sexual dynamics of love (Eros). He lists the sexual practices that are omnipresent in nature and suggests that the notion of women's property was born during the [[Sedentism|sedentarization]] of the [[Neolithic era]]. It also details the complexity of sexual systems, which are often designed to frame the reproductive rules of each species.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Didier Vincent: "Baisez et tout ira mieux"|url=http://www.sinemensuel.com/interview/jean-didier-vincent-baisez-et-tout-ira-mieux/|website=Sinemensuel.com|date=July 2015|access-date=21 January 2016}}</ref>

In his book ''Bienvenue en Transhumanie'', he takes a sceptical look at [[transhumanism]], denouncing a lack of morality that is necessary around this radical transformation of the [[genome]]. He fears a disconnection between reproduction and sexuality, and that sexuality is virtualized by directly stimulating the affected parts of the brain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Didier Vincent, de l'humain au transhumain|url=http://www.lepoint.fr/grands-entretiens/jean-didier-vincent-de-l-humain-au-transhumain-13-10-2011-1386477_326.php|author=Élisabeth Lévy|website=Lepoint.fr|date=13 October 2011|access-date=21 January 2017}}</ref>

* Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]

== Awards and honours {{citation needed|date=May 2020}} ==
* 1981: La Caze Prize from the Academy of Sciences
* 1991: Blaise-Pascal prize
* 1996: Medicine and Culture Award from the Institute of Health Sciences
* 1998: Gold medal at the University of Prague
* 1999: Doctor honoris causa of the Free University of Brussels
* 2010: Honorary President of the Société historique et archéologique de Libourne
* Officer of the [[Legion of Honour|Légion d'Honneur]]
* Commander of the [[Ordre des Palmes académiques|Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]
* Knight of the [[Order of Agricultural Merit|Ordre du Mérite Agricole]]

== Polemics ==

=== On Down's syndrome ===
On 5 October 2012, during the programme ''La Tête au carré'', broadcast on [[France Inter]], a new test likely to diagnose [[Down syndrome]] in early pregnancy was discussed. Vincent defended this prenatal diagnosis, claiming that "Down's syndrome is a poison in a family. " During the programme, Jean-Didier Vincent revisited this statement, which was considered "violent" by host Mathieu Vidard, and withdrew it, calling it an "unfortunate term" but without apologizing.{{citation needed|date=May 2020}} [[Éléonore Laloux]], a young woman with Down syndrome and spokesperson for the collective Les Amis d'Éléonore, responded to the biologist in 2013 in a video<ref>[https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x177y8o_journee-de-la-trisomie-21-eleonore-laloux-s-exprime_webcam Eléonore Laloux répond à Jean-Didier Vincent]</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Non, les trisomiques ne sont pas un "poison dans une famille" !|url=http://www.lavie.fr/actualite/billets/non-les-trisomiques-ne-sont-pas-un-poison-dans-une-famille-13-11-2012-33238_288.php|author=Emmanuel Laloux|website=Lavie.fr|date=12 November 2012|access-date=21 January 2017|language=fr}}</ref> and in March 2014 in her autobiography {{Lang|fr|Triso et alors!}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Handicap.fr |date=2014-03-21 |title=Eléonore, trisomique, publie son livre : Triso, et alors ! |url=https://informations.handicap.fr/a--6738.php |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Handicap.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

=== On GMOs ===
During the same programme, Vincent defended the firm [[Monsanto]] and made the following comments: "we must use [[Genetically modified organism|GMOs]]", "it has rendered great services to agriculture", "it has increased productivity."{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}

=== Conviction ===
On 12 February 2008, during the television show ''Ce soir ou jamais'', he said about [[Jean-Marie Le Pen]]: "We knew him as the white wolf, he was a bastard", and added: "he probably committed crimes, but I can't say it on the air". On 28 May 2009, the Paris Court of Appeal found him guilty of insult (first sentence) and defamation (second sentence), and sentenced him to a suspended fine of €1,500 and €4,000.<ref>Libération, 28 mai 2009 [http://www.liberation.fr/societe/0101570013-5500-euros-pour-avoir-traite-le-pen-de-salopard « 5500 euros pour avoir traité Le Pen de salopard »] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090531053535/http://www.liberation.fr/societe/0101570013-5500-euros-pour-avoir-traite-le-pen-de-salopard |date=2009-05-31 }}</ref>
